course_name_en: Applied Mechanics 2: Dynamics and Strength of Materials

learning_outcomes.text: The student can quantitatively describe the kinematics and dynamics of rigid bodies in space and in planar motion. He/she uses concepts such as the instantaneous rotation vector and instantaneous rotational acceleration vector, the impulse and the angular momentum of rigid bodies.

The student masters the elementary concepts of strength of materials (section forces and moments, stresses and strains, defined in a three-dimensional space) and can apply them in simple concrete situations. He/she knows the equilibrium equations as a function of stresses, the relationships between displacements and deformations (strains and shear angles), and the relationships between stresses and deformations via material laws (Hooke's law). He/she knows the concept of elastic deformation energy and the derived expressions as a function of stresses and deformations.
The student can, through practicing the subject matter, achieve independent mastery and application in technical problem situations.

syllabus_topics: Kinematics of objects in spatial motion
Instantaneous rotation vector and rotational acceleration vector
Velocity and acceleration of points of an object and of a composite structure
Relative motion
Dynamics of objects in spatial motion
Dynamics of material systems (with attention to the center of mass of a system/object), with attention to the concepts of impulse (new compared to the previous version) and angular momentum
Equations of motion for an object in space (with a brief treatment of planar motion)
Application of dynamics in non-inertial reference frames for material systems
Exercises on sub-aspects of mechanics
Kinematics of objects in spatial motion
Dynamics of objects in spatial motion
Relative motion and inertial forces for material systems
Online integrated case exercise
The concepts of stresses and deformations, basic data for structural engineering designs, are defined in a three-dimensional space
Equilibrium equations as a function of stresses
Relationships between displacements and deformations (strains and shear angles)
Relationships between stresses and deformations via material laws (Hooke's law)
Elastic deformation energy
Derived expressions for elastic deformation energy as a function of stresses and deformations
Transition from external forces to force effects on a section (section forces) through a beam-shaped body
Reduction of section forces to simple combinations of normal and shear forces, bending moments and torsional moments
Simple relationships between section forces and the stresses occurring at a point of these sections, with superposition when multiple types of section forces act on the section
Deformations derived from material laws
Exercises on the basic concepts and theory of Strength of Materials
Calculation of section forces for simple, statically determinate two- and three-dimensional structures based on external loading
Study of stresses and deformations over the cross-section for each of the four elementary section force types
Superposition of stresses and deformations
